instructions.introduction: Imagine you’re planning and booking a trip with an AI assistant. We’re studying which parts of the process you’d want the assistant to handle, how you want the assistant to handle them, and which parts you’d prefer to do yourself. (The AI assistant isn’t perfect and it may break sometimes…how would you like that handled?) For each task, we’ll give you the trip details and tell you what you need to prioritize, and you choose the AI response you’d prefer in that situation. The study will be broken down into three portions:

steps.title: Planning your trip:
steps.text: Choose how you’d find and select flights, then a hotel and room/rate together. Complete all flight scenarios before all hotel scenarios.

steps.title: Preparing your reservations:
steps.text: This is where you decide how you’d like to get the flight, hotel, and rental car reservations added to cart/ready for payment.

steps.title: Completing the purchase:
steps.text: This is where you decide how you’d want to pay for the trip.

instructions.note: First, choose flights across four budget and schedule scenarios. Then choose hotel/room/rate packages across the same four conditions, followed by flight reservation preparation. All travel details are fictional; you and the chatbot can search the same options. Nothing is actually reserved or paid for. Treat each task independently. Choose a chatbot approach or Do it yourself, or describe another approach. Click Start Study to begin.

introduction.text: Imagine planning a solo trip to Boston. Use the budget and schedule for the part of the trip you are answering about.

summary.value: $350 total, including taxes and one checked bag

summary.label: Hotel task assumptions
summary.value: Independent of flight answers. Three nights; private room and bathroom. Prefer Boston Common proximity and free cancellation; may trade these for savings. Flexible stays can shift the whole trip without extra transportation cost.

checkpoints.title: Finding and choosing a flight

context.text: You’re flying alone from Chicago (ORD) to Boston (BOS) this Friday for a vacation. Your return flight is already arranged.
All flights are nonstop economy. Prices include taxes and one checked bag. Airlines are equally acceptable, with the same cancellation terms. Times are local: CT for departure and ET for arrival.
Preference: Save money, but you would prefer departing between 10 a.m. and noon. Choosing a flight does not reserve or purchase it.
Requirements: $350 maximum, including taxes and one checked bag. Depart Friday between 9 a.m. and noon CT.
How would you prefer to find and choose your flight?

checkpoints.taskInstruction: Ask for help finding and choosing a flight.
checkpoints.question: How would you prefer to find and choose your flight?
checkpoints.followUp: Why this approach? If none fits, what would you prefer?

options.text:

I search for flights, compare them, and choose one without the chatbot.

Chatbot searches; I choose

- HarborLink Airways HL 112 | ORD 9:10 a.m. CT → BOS 12:30 p.m. ET | $320 total
- Lakefront Air LF 222 | ORD 11:20 a.m. CT → BOS 2:40 p.m. ET | $345 total

Compare them and choose one. I have not ranked or recommended either flight.

Chatbot recommends a shortlist; I choose

checkpoints.title: Preparing the reservation

context.text: For this question, assume Lakefront Air LF 222 has already been selected, regardless of your previous answer. It departs Chicago O’Hare at 11:20 a.m. CT and arrives at Boston Logan at 2:40 p.m. ET. The $345 fare includes one checked bag.

The reservation form asks for your legal name, date of birth, contact information, optional frequent-flyer number, checked-bag count, and seat selection. For this exercise, imagine you have these details saved in a travel profile, including a Lakefront Air frequent-flyer number and an aisle-seat preference. Seats 14A (window) and 14C (aisle) are both available at no extra cost. Use the fictional profile for this exercise. Do not enter your real information.
How would you prefer to prepare the reservation?

checkpoints.title: Finding and choosing a hotel and room

context.text: Choose your hotel, room, and rate together.

You’re visiting Boston alone for three nights. You need a private room and bathroom. Prefer staying near Boston Common and having free cancellation, but consider giving these up to save money. All packages meet your basic room requirements; prices cover the whole stay, including taxes and fees.

items: Budget: $600 maximum for all three nights.

context.text: This hotel task is independent of your flight answers. All details are fictional. No reservation or payment is made.
